risks.risk: Gears may be misaligned, jammed, or the derailleur hanger may be bent.
risks.proof: A video clip of the bike being pedaled on a stand or while riding, shifting through all gear combinations.
risks.if_unproven: as having a non-functional gear system

risks.risk: Disc brakes may be contaminated, worn out, or require bleeding (if hydraulic).
risks.proof: A video showing the bike being ridden and coming to a complete, sharp stop using both brakes.
risks.if_unproven: as needing a full brake system overhaul

risks.risk: Front suspension fork may be seized or have leaking seals.
risks.proof: A video of a person pushing down on the handlebars to demonstrate smooth compression and rebound of the fork.

risks.risk: The frame may have hairline cracks, especially near the welds or bottom bracket.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the frame joints and the underside of the bottom bracket.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the model number (usually located on the top tube or near the seat post).
Video of the gears shifting through all 18 speeds.
Video demonstrating the front suspension travel.
Close-up photos of the tire treads and brake discs.
response.reason: The bicycle is clearly identified as a Rockrider mountain bike with disc brakes. While the exact model number is not legible, the brand and visible components allow for a baseline valuation at the worst-case mechanical condition.
